verdict.rationale: The evidence documents a managed scaling path: Elastic Cloud Serverless autoscales resources, absorbs ingest spikes, and separates search and index tiers so they scale independently. Self-managed and Elastic-managed deployment options exist, and a community user recommends Elastic Cloud on Kubernetes for running clusters. Clustering is only implied ("instead of managing clusters, nodes, data tiers"), and a community reference to the Jepsen analysis says indexed documents can be lost during network partitions, which is a caveat on high availability. Missing for 10: explicit clustering/sharding docs, replica and high-availability configuration docs, evidence of scale to hundreds of millions of documents, independent corroboration of HA reliability.
